To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

variants in PIK3CA (rs1183319) and KCNMB (rs7645550) are associated with insulin sensitivity in two populations of different ancesties and that these associations are modified by the ratio of n-3 to n-6 fatty acids in the diet.

the PIK3CA–KCNMB3 genetic variants rs7645550 and rs1183319 are associated with insulin sensitivity, and their associations with insulin resistance are modulated by dietary PUFA in populations of different ancestry.

the genetic association between the PIK3CA/KCNMB3 region and insulin resistance, measured by homeostasis model of assessment of insulin resistance, is modified by the ratio of n-3/n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the PIK3CA gene and KCNMB gene in the development of insulin resistance.
the role of the PIK3CA gene in type 2 diabetes (T2D).
the association of PIK3R1 and KCNMB2 with type 2 diabetes mellitus and insulin resistance, respectively.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic association between PIK3A-KCNMB3 and glucose-related phenotypes was modified by dietary PUFAs in two different population.
the PIK3CA KCNMB3 genetic variants are associated with glucose homeostasis in populations of different ancestry and that this association may be modified by dietary PUFAs.
PUFA modulate insulin resistance in the context of genetic variants in PIK3CA, but the exact mechanisms of this interaction need further study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic variants of KCNMB3 and PIK3CA are associated with insulin sensitivity and that these associations are modulated by n-3:6 PUFA intake.
the genetic variants in PIK3CA or KCNMB3 may be associated with insulin resistance.
the genetic associations between PIK3A-KCNMB3 and insulin resistance are modulated by dietary n-3 PUFA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetic variants in this region may be associated with insulin resistance and diabetes in the general population and that this association can be modulated by dietary fat.
dietary PUFA may modulate the genetic associations between PIK3RCA-KCNMB genetic variants and insulin resistance.
dietary n-3 and n-6 fatty acids can modulate the effect of genetic variants on insulin resistance.
